item.text:
Invariant: for each SKU, committed reservations plus shipped units never exceed physical inventory. Every reservation has a unique ID and monotonically versioned state; all messages are idempotent, and stale or duplicate messages cannot revive canceled reservations.

Each SKU has a single authoritative owner region at a time. Ownership is leased with an epoch; only the owner may commit reservations or shipments. During a partition, the non-owner may accept provisional, non-guaranteed holds, but cannot promise availability. Payment authorization is likewise provisional until the owner commits it.

The requirement that must be relaxed is accepting guaranteed reservations in both isolated regions. Otherwise strict no-oversell and immediate irreversible shipping are impossible without coordination or over-allocation.

Commit protocol: the owner atomically records the reservation, payment intent, and inventory decrement in a durable log, then emits a commit event. Shipping may become irreversible only after receiving that commit and confirming the matching epoch and reservation ID. Payment capture occurs after reservation commit, with compensating refund if shipping fails.

On recovery, regions exchange durable logs, deduplicate by IDs, discard stale epochs, and reconcile provisional holds. Uncommitted holds expire or are canceled; payment authorizations are voided/refunded. Conflicting shipment requests are rejected before dispatch. If an unauthorized region shipped despite the rule, the protocol cannot undo it; it records an invariant violation and requires business compensation.
